title: Kits Ready to Go Further
panelPrompt: Click a kit to see what it does and what a mentor would see.

image.style: flat vector comparison poster, clean hardware illustrations, muted textbook palette
image.overall: A two-column comparison poster about two advanced coding club kits. Each column is a tall rounded panel with a coloured header bar carrying its printed title, and a clean flat illustration of the kit below it. The two printed headers, and the ONLY text in the image, are: "Signal Processing Kit" (left) and "Smartwatch / Wearable Display Kit" (right).
image.layoutNotes: Divide the content area into 2 equal-width vertical columns with a clear gutter of background between each pair. Every column must have the SAME width, top edge, and bottom edge so the overlay's hover zones line up exactly. Each column has its printed header in bold dark text at the very top, on a tinted header bar in that column's accent colour, with simple flat icons below. No other text anywhere. Leave at least 4% margin at the left and right edges and 8% at top and bottom. With only two columns each panel is wide, so draw one larger central illustration per column rather than a cluster of small icons.

zones.label: Signal Processing Kit
zones.summary: Turns raw sound into a live, moving frequency display -- no math required to run it.
facts: Builds on the microphone and sound spectrum kits from Chapter 20
Updates its display many times per second (real-time audio processing)
Uses a technique called the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) behind the scenes
The maths itself is covered in the companion Signal Processing on a $5 MicroController textbook, not here

draw.position: The left column, roughly 3% to 48% of the image width.
draw.visual: Header bar tinted blue. Below it: a small breadboard with a microcontroller and a tiny microphone module, wired to a small rectangular screen showing a bar-graph spectrum of about a dozen vertical bars of varying heights. No numbers or axis marks on the screen.

zones.label: Smartwatch / Wearable Display Kit
zones.summary: A display kit built to be worn, not set on a desk.
facts: Extends the Chapter 20 display kit idea onto wrist-wearable hardware
Battery power draw matters far more than on a stationary kit
Connections must survive real movement, not just sit on a breadboard
The companion Clocks and Watches textbook covers an extensive set of wearable projects

draw.position: The right column, roughly 52% to 97% of the image width.
draw.visual: Header bar tinted amber. Below it: a wrist-worn device with a fabric strap and a small round screen showing simple abstract shapes (no digits), plus a small flat battery icon and a coiled flexible wire suggesting movement tolerance.

quiz.question: Which kit turns sound into a moving frequency display?
